solution.excerpt:
Order Stuck - CHECKED_INVALID - SA261007-06814792
Generated: 2026-10-20

Issue:
Order SA261007-06814792 is stuck at CHECKED_INVALID status. The order was placed on 2026-10-07 at 07:25:49 in the SA (Saudi Arabia) store using Tabby (BNPL) as the payment mode for a total of 7528.04 SAR. No consignments were ever created - the order never passed the check phase.

RCA:
The order failed validation at the checkOrder action in the order-process-v25-69 business process. Both order process instances (code suffixes ...215721 and ...215724) are in FAILED state, with 50 ProcessTaskLog entries all at the checkOrder actionId.

The code path is: CheckOrderAction.executeAction() calls DefaultCheckOrderService.check(), which runs four validation checks in sequence: (1) order.calculated must be true, (2) order.entries must not be empty, (3) order.paymentInfo must not be null, (4) checkDeliveryOptions() must pass.

DB verification confirms: calculated=1 (true), paymentInfo is populated (PK 9465372803114), and order entries exist. However, order.deliveryMode is NULL. The checkDeliveryOptions() method in DefaultCheckOrderService checks: if order.getDeliveryMode() == null, it then iterates order entries looking for any non-service entry with a null deliveryMode - if found, it returns false, logging "Order entry delivery mode is null".

When check() returns false, CheckOrderAction.executeAction() sets the order status to CHECKED_INVALID and returns Transition.NOK, which causes the business process to fail.

The root cause is that the order's deliveryMode was never set during checkout. This typically happens when the delivery mode assignment step in the checkout flow fails or is skipped - the order is created and payment is authorized (two PaymentTransaction entries with ACCEPTED status for 7528.04 SAR via Tabby), but the delivery mode is not persisted before the order process reaches the checkOrder action.

Possible remediation:
1. Set the correct delivery mode on the order via HAC Groovy script. Query the available delivery modes for the SA store and link the appropriate one to the order (matching what was selected during checkout, which may be recoverable from the cart/session data or order entry delivery groups).
2. Once deliveryMode is set, restart the failed order process from the checkOrder action to re-run the validation. The process should now pass the checkDeliveryOptions() check, set the order to CHECKED_VALID, and proceed to consignment creation.
3. Alternatively, if the delivery mode cannot be determined, cancel the order and reverse the Tabby payment authorization.

Reference: PC-52605 (process-restart, REUSABLE) contains a script for retriggering business processes stuck at ERROR. The deliveryMode set + process restart approach is the standard remediation for CHECKED_INVALID caused by missing deliveryMode.

## Remediation
- Root cause: NULL deliveryMode on order causing checkDeliveryOptions() failure in DefaultCheckOrderService.check()
- Remediation type: Set deliveryMode + restart order process
- Reusable PC ticket: PC-52605 (process-restart, REUSABLE)
- Status: RCA saved, awaiting user review

Stuck order on Hybris — 13 TR-region orders across 6 error categories
Generated: 2026-10-16T00:00:00

Issue:
TKME-2381 reports 13 stuck TR-region orders across 6 distinct error categories. All orders were created on 2026/10/14-15 and are stuck at various stages of the order fulfillment process. The error breakdown is as follows:

1. splitOrder ERROR — 5 orders (TR261015-16842055, TR261015-16805269, TR261008-08332438, TR261003-02929746, TR261002-01958606): All at WAITING_FOR_SEND_FINANCIAL status. The order process errors at the splitOrder action with "missing values for [warehouse] in model ConsignmentModel () to create a new Consignment" thrown by de.hybris.platform.servicelayer.interceptor.impl.MandatoryAttributesValidator. This means when the order process attempts to split the order into consignments, the warehouse attribute on the newly created ConsignmentModel is null. The MandatoryAttributesValidator intercepts the save and rejects it because warehouse is a mandatory attribute on ConsignmentModel. This is a known pattern — Jira cross-reference found PC-55386 (AEME-6614) and PC-54279, both closed, where the fix was a manual BackOffice retrigger of the order process from the splitOrder action node. The retrigger re-executes the split logic and, on second attempt, the warehouse assignment succeeds.

2. sendConsignmentToWarehouse ERROR — 3 orders (TR261003-03360414, TR261014-16036338, TR261009-09297116): All at ORDER_SPLIT status. The consignment process errors at sendConsignmentToWarehouse with "I/O error: Connection reset; nested exception is java.net.SocketException: Connection reset". This is a NERP integration connectivity issue — Hybris sends consignment data to the warehouse via NERP, and the connection is reset mid-transfer. This is a well-documented known issue in the TR tenant. Jira cross-reference found TKME-2343 (closed, 12 TR orders with identical error), TKME-2308 (closed, 21 orders), and PM-658 (global NERP I/O tracking). PC-55336 deployed an autoheal cronjob (autoheal-tr-IOErroredOrdersRemediationCronJob) that runs every 4 hours in PROD, finds errored consignment processes with I/O error patterns, and restarts them from sendConsignmentToWarehouse. These 3 orders should be auto-remediated by the autoheal if it is running.

3. isAdditionalInfoCollected ERROR — 2 orders (TR261015-16768317, TR261015-16672509): Both at SHIPPED status. The consignment process errors at isAdditionalInfoCollected with "I/O error: Connection reset; nested exception is java.net.SocketException: Connection reset". Same NERP connectivity root cause as Category 2 — the autoheal cronjob PC-55336 explicitly handles isAdditionalInfoCollected as well. These should also be auto-remediated.

4. completeFinancialUpdate ERROR — 1 order (TR261011-11999937): At WAITING_FOR_FINANCIAL status. The order process errors at completeFinancialUpdate with "I/O error: Read timed out; nested exception is java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out". This is a NERP response timeout — NERP takes too long to respond during the financial update step and Hybris times out. PM-658 explicitly lists completeFinancialUpdate as one of 8 actions affected by NERP I/O errors. PC-30574 (closed) updated the failedAndErrorOrdersJob Groovy script with action mapping: completeFinancialUpdate maps to completeFinancialUpdate for retrigger. The order process needs to be restarted from the completeFinancialUpdate action.

5. REFUND_FAILED — 1 order (TR261015-16770938): At REFUND_FAILED status. The payment entry status is REFUND_FOLLOW_ON:ERROR. This indicates the refund follow-on transaction was attempted but the payment gateway returned an ERROR status. No reusable PC ticket was found in the TR region for REFUND_FOLLOW_ON:ERROR — this is the first occurrence of this specific refund error type in TR. This requires payment team investigation to determine the gateway-side reason for the rejection before a retrigger can be attempted.

6. commitStock ERROR — 1 order (TR261011-11725431): At SHIPPED status. The consignment process errors at commitStock with "no stock level for product [TURKEY-B2C-SMP-Tier5-ADH-24M] found in warehouse name [D2C MX] warehouse code [WC17-S751]". The product has no StockLevel entry in warehouse WC17-S751 (D2C MX). Without a stock level record, the commitStock action cannot reserve stock and the process errors. Jira cross-reference found TKME-2322 (closed, exact same warehouse + product pattern for a different Tier product) and GMT-21026 (parent GMT ticket). The established remediation is two-step: (1) ImpEx to create or update StockLevel for the product in warehouse WC17-S751 with forceInStock status (reusable from PC-52623), then (2) restart the consignment process from the commitStock action node (reusable from PC-52825 / PC-55096).

Kibana was unavailable during this investigation (browser extension relay inactive). HAC authenticated successfully but flexsearch queries timed out. The error information above was sourced from the ticket description and Aryan's remediation comment, which contain the exact error messages extracted from the system. Jira cross-reference was performed successfully with 18 highly relevant resolved tickets found.

RCA:
The root causes fall into three distinct categories:

NERP Integration I/O Errors (Categories 2, 3, 4 — 6 orders): The TR tenant experiences intermittent NERP connectivity issues where connections are reset (SocketException: Connection reset) or time out (SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out) during warehouse communication. NERP is the middleware that handles warehouse integration for the TR region. When Hybris sends data to NERP (consignment data at sendConsignmentToWarehouse, additional info at isAdditionalInfoCollected, financial data at completeFinancialUpdate), NERP occasionally drops the connection or fails to respond within the timeout window. This is a known systemic issue tracked under PM-658 and PM-711 (global), with autoheal cronjobs deployed (PC-55336 for TR). The root cause is on the NERP/network infrastructure side, not in Hybris code.

Missing Warehouse on ConsignmentModel (Category 1 — 5 orders): The splitOrder action in the order process creates new ConsignmentModel instances. The MandatoryAttributesValidator rejects the save because the warehouse attribute is null. This occurs when the warehouse assignment logic during order split fails to resolve a warehouse for the consignment. The retrigger pattern (manual BO retrigger from splitOrder) works because the second attempt re-evaluates the warehouse assignment and succeeds — suggesting a transient data resolution issue rather than a configuration gap. Established pattern from PC-55386 and PC-54279.

Missing Stock Level (Category 6 — 1 order): The product TURKEY-B2C-SMP-Tier5-ADH-24M has no StockLevel record in warehouse WC17-S751 (D2C MX). The commitStock action requires a stock level to reserve inventory. Without the record, the action fails. This is a master data issue — the stock level was never created for this product-warehouse combination. Same pattern as TKME-2322 (closed).

Payment Gateway Rejection (Category 5 — 1 order): The refund follow-on payment transaction entry returned ERROR status from the payment gateway. This is a gateway-side rejection, not a Hybris code issue. The specific reason for the rejection needs to be determined from the payment gateway logs before a retrigger can be safely attempted.

Possible remediation:

Categories 2 and 3 (5 orders, sendConsignmentToWarehouse + isAdditionalInfoCollected I/O errors): Verify that the PC-55336 autoheal cronjob is running. If it is, these 5 orders should be auto-remediated within the next 4-hour cycle. If the autoheal is not running or these orders persist after the next cycle, a manual retrigger of the consignment processes from their respective error action nodes is needed. No new PC ticket required — reuse PC-55336.

Category 1 (5 orders, splitOrder missing warehouse): Manual BackOffice retrigger of the order process from the splitOrder action node for all 5 orders. This is the established pattern from PC-55386 and PC-54279. A new PC ticket is needed for this batch.

Category 4 (1 order, completeFinancialUpdate timeout): Restart the order process from completeFinancialUpdate action. The failedAndErrorOrdersJob script from PC-30574 has the action mapping for this. Can reuse PC-30574 or create a new PC ticket.

Category 5 (1 order, REFUND_FAILED): Requires payment team investigation to determine the gateway-side reason for REFUND_FOLLOW_ON:ERROR before retrigger. No Hybris-side fix can be applied blindly without understanding why the gateway rejected the refund.

Category 6 (1 order, commitStock no stock level): Two-step remediation — (1) ImpEx to create StockLevel for TURKEY-B2C-SMP-Tier5-ADH-24M in warehouse WC17-S751 with forceInStock status (reuse PC-52623 pattern), (2) restart consignment process from commitStock action (reuse PC-52825 / PC-55096 pattern). Business confirmation needed on whether this product should have stock in D2C MX warehouse.

## Remediation

Reusable PC tickets:
- PC-55336 (Closed, REUSABLE): Autoheal cronjob for TR I/O errored orders — handles sendConsignmentToWarehouse + isAdditionalInfoCollected
- PC-55386 (Closed): splitOrder missing warehouse — manual BO retrigger pattern
- PC-54279 (Closed): splitOrder missing warehouse — same pattern
- PC-30574 (Closed): failedAndErrorOrdersJob — completeFinancialUpdate action mapping
- PC-52623 (Closed): ImpEx StockLevel update for commitStock
- PC-52825 (Closed): Groovy restart from commitStock after stock fix
- PC-55096 (Closed): Batch commitStock process restart script
- PC-46275 (Closed): Earlier autoheal for omnichannel I/O errors (superseded by PC-55336)

No reusable PC ticket found for REFUND_FAILED / REFUND_FOLLOW_ON:ERROR in TR region.

solution.excerpt:
Ticket: MHME-1466 - Unit limitations for Orange Platform EPP
Generated: 2026-10-16T11:30:00Z

Issue:
The reporter (Ashwani) has requested updating the product purchase limits per division for each account on the Orange Platform EPP store (ma_orange) in Morocco. Specifically, Mobile division products should be capped at a maximum of 5 units per account, and VD (Visual Display) division products should also be capped at 5 units per account. No purchase limits are currently configured for the ma_orange store on the platform.

RCA:
The ma_orange BaseSite exists in the Hybris database (confirmed via HAC query: uid=ma_orange, locale=en). It is one of 18 Morocco-region stores including ma_corporates, ma_students, ma_samsung_socgen, and others. The purchase limit mechanism in the Samsung Toko platform operates through two Hybris types defined in tokomultistorecore-items.xml:

1. TokoCategoryPurchaseLimit (table: tokocatpurchaselimits, typecode 10714) — linked to TokoMultiStore via TokoMultiStore2CategoryPurchaseLimitRelation (1:N). Fields: category (Category, required, unique), quantityThreshold (Integer), valueThreshold (Double), userGroup (UserGroup, optional), defaultLimit (boolean, default false). This type enforces per-category quantity limits on a multistore, optionally scoped to a specific user group.

2. UserPurchaseLimit (table: userpurchaselimit, typecode 10716) — linked to TokoMultiStore via TokoMultiStore2UserPurchaseLimitRelation (1:N). Fields: value (Double, required), defaultLimit (boolean, default false), userGroup (UserGroup, optional, unique). This type enforces cart-level purchase value limits per user group on a multistore.

The validation is triggered by TokoCartFacadeImpl.validateProductQuantityPurchaseLimits() (line 2409 in TokoCartFacadeImpl.java), which delegates to productPurchaseLimitValidationStrategy.validateCart(). This is called from CartsController.java (line 1100) and BaseCommerceController.java (line 578) during cart validation. The controller checks the result for MULTISTORE_CART_PURCHASE_LIMIT and MULTISTORE_PURCHASE_LIMIT error codes to surface validation messages to the user.

Additionally, CategoryDivisionMapping (typecode 11351, defined in tokocore-items.xml) maps category codes to division identifiers (field: categoryDivision of type CategoryDivisionParametersMapping). However, no CategoryDivisionMapping entries exist in the database currently. The knox.productbenefit.division.config.enabled.in config property is set to true but the .in suffix indicates this is India-only and does not apply to Morocco.

No TokoConfigProperty entries exist for ma_orange related to purchase limits, cart limits, or unit limits. The config properties toko.cart.purchase.limit.validation.enabled.in and toko.purchase.limit.exclusion.order.status.in are India-specific (the .in suffix denotes India region). The global properties populate.product.purchase.limit.disabled=true and product.purchase.limit.for.user.disabled=true indicate that purchase limit population is currently disabled globally, though the validation infrastructure is present.

This is a configuration request, not a platform bug or code defect. The Hybris type system already supports the requested behaviour through TokoCategoryPurchaseLimit entries linked to the ma_orange TokoMultiStore, with the Mobile and VD categories mapped to quantityThreshold=5 each. No code changes are required.

Possible remediation:
This requires an ImpEx script to configure purchase limits on the ma_orange store. The steps are:

1. Identify the TokoMultiStore PK for ma_orange (the BaseSite uid is ma_orange, but the TokoMultiStore may use a different identifier — this needs verification in the database).

2. Identify the Category PKs for Mobile division and VD division products in the Morocco product catalog. If Mobile and VD do not exist as standalone Category items, the appropriate parent categories for these divisions need to be identified.

3. Create TokoCategoryPurchaseLimit entries via ImpEx:
   - One entry linking the Mobile category to the ma_orange TokoMultiStore with quantityThreshold=5
   - One entry linking the VD category to the ma_orange TokoMultiStore with quantityThreshold=5
   - If per-account (per-user-group) scoping is needed, set the userGroup field on each TokoCategoryPurchaseLimit entry to the specific Orange Platform account user groups

4. Ensure the config property toko.cart.purchase.limit.validation.enabled is set for the ma_orange site (or globally) so the validation is active.

5. Verify in Backoffice that the limits appear on the ma_orange multistore configuration and test with a cart containing more than 5 units of a Mobile division product to confirm the validation blocks the checkout.

No PC ticket or HAC Groovy script is needed for this change — it is an ImpEx configuration update that should be applied through the standard Backoffice or ImpEx import process.

# RCA: SAME-4035
Ticket Summary: Stuck order on Hybris - SA261019-21102217
Generated: 2026-10-20T19:30:00.000Z

Issue:
Order SA261019-21102217 (SA region, Tabby payment, 2069.10 SAR) is stuck at ORDER_SPLIT status. The single consignment SA261019-21102217 is at WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER and has never been transmitted to warehouse WC05. Payment was fully captured (2069.10 SAR via Tabby) on 2026-10-19 12:11:35. The consignment business process (consignment-process-v11-36) is in ERROR state at the sendConsignmentToWarehouse action node.

RCA:
The consignment process executed all pre-check actions successfully: isReadyForFulfillment returned OK, isSentAsBatch returned YES, waitForSendToWarehouse returned OK, and sendConsignmentToExternalERP returned OK. The process then reached the sendConsignmentToWarehouse action, which transmits the consignment data to the warehouse system (SAP/GERP integration). During this call, the HTTP connection to the warehouse endpoint was reset mid-transfer (java.net.SocketException: Connection reset / I/O error).

The ProcessTaskLog for this action shows an empty returnCode, which confirms an unhandled exception was thrown rather than a normal error return. The consignment process transitioned to ERROR state with endMessage "An error occurred while executing the process."

The order process (order-process-v25-69) remains in RUNNING state but is blocked at the waitForConsignmentProcess gate. It cannot advance until the consignment process completes successfully. Generated: 2026-10-19T10:30:00.000Z

## Issue

Order SA260916-85802827 (SA region, Tabby payment, 3419.10 SAR) has a SIT Return detected on the sizing kit consignment (SA260916-85802827_1) but the refund has not been processed. The order is stuck at SHIPPED status with the order process blocked at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd.

## RCA

Hi [~arjenelle.a@samsung.com] ,

The order has two consignments: the main consignment (SM-S938BZTOMEA, status COMPLETED since Oct 10) and the sizing kit consignment (ET-YQ500KBEGWW, consignment code SA260916-85802827_1, still at SHIPPED).

On Oct 19, GERP detected a SIT Return on the sizing kit consignment and logged "Consignment [SA260916-85802827_1] contains SIT Return. Marking it as COMPLETED" at both 09:48:41 and 10:18:37 UTC. However, the consignment status in the database remained SHIPPED. Kibana confirms the consignment was "updated from [SHIPPED] to [SHIPPED]", meaning no actual status transition occurred despite the log message.

The consignment process for the sizing kit (order-process-v25-69-SA260916-85802827-1789579486159_2, definition consignment-process-v11-36) is still in RUNNING state. The shipping readiness check returned NOK both times, preventing the consignment process from advancing. The order process (order-process-v25-69) is blocked at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd/isProcessCompleted, waiting for all consignment processes to complete before proceeding.

No ReturnRequest was created in the system. Without a ReturnRequest, no ReturnRequestProcess was initiated, and therefore no refund flow was triggered. The payment transactions show only AUTHORIZATION and CAPTURE entries (3419.10 SAR captured on Sep 16) with no refund or reversal entries.

The BILLING-CALLBACK-RECEIVED process parameter warning ("Process parameter with name BILLING-CALLBACK-RECEIVED does not exist") appeared during both SIT Return detection cycles, indicating the billing callback required for the process to advance was never registered.

No ERROR-level logs were found in Kibana for this order. The failure is silent — the SIT Return was detected but the consignment status update did not persist, blocking the entire downstream flow without throwing any exception.

This is the same pattern documented in UAME-3621 (SIT Return present but refund not processed) and matches the SAME-3941 remediation scenario.

## Possible Remediation

1. Manually update the sizing kit consignment (SA260916-85802827_1) status from SHIPPED to COMPLETED to align with the GERP SIT Return detection.
2. Restart the stuck consignment process _2 (order-process-v25-69-SA260916-85802827-1789579486159_2) so it advances past the shipping check.
3. This should unblock the order process at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd, allowing it to complete and trigger the refund flow.
4. If the order process completion alone does not trigger the refund, a ReturnRequest may need to be created manually with sitReturn=true, followed by triggering the return-refund process.

PC-52765 (script-SAME-3941-sa260722-return-refund-retrigger.groovy) was reviewed but cannot be reused directly because it requires an existing ReturnRequestProcess, and this order has no ReturnRequest at all. A new script would be needed if manual consignment completion does not auto-trigger the refund.

Thanks,

Aryan

2. customersupportagentgroup — "CS Agent Group" — grants CS Agent Group views and Assisted Service Module access. Inherits employeegroup and customersupportagentrole.
3. customersupportmanagergroup — inherits customersupportagentgroup plus manager-level roles.
4. customersupportadministratorgroup — inherits all of the above plus administrator roles.

The 5 patterns are:

The consignment process (consignment-process-v11-36) reached the sendConsignmentToWarehouse action node, which calls SendConsignmentToWarehouseAction.executeAction() (com.samsung.toko.fulfilmentprocess.actions.consignment.SendConsignmentToWarehouseAction, line 38). This delegates to TokoBifrostWarehouseAdapterImpl.sendConsignmentToWarehouse() (line 217), which converts the consignment to a Bifrost sales order request via tokoBifrostSalesOrderRequestConverter and sends it to the WMS through TokoBifrostWebClient.

The WMS endpoint dropped the TCP connection mid-request (java.net.SocketException: Connection reset), causing the process engine to catch the RuntimeException at ActionNode.handleActionExecutionRuntimeException (line 163) and set the consignment process to ERROR state.

DB verification confirms all 6 orders have:
- Order process: RUNNING (waiting for warehouse subprocess to end)
- Consignment process: ERROR (consignment-process-v11-36)
- Consignment status: WAITING_FOR_TRANSFER (no tracking, no shipping date, no GERP bill)
- Payment: AUTH and CAPTURE both ACCEPTED

Orders TR260926-95689021 and TR260925-94199293 are partial - one consignment completed successfully and one is stuck. The stuck consignments in these orders also have ERROR state on their consignment processes.

4 of 6 stuck consignments route to warehouse WC17-S751 (cross-dock), 2 route to DIVA warehouses (ce-xdock). The Connection reset is a transient network-level failure between Hybris and the WMS/Bifrost integration layer, not a code defect.

This is a recurring platform issue confirmed by Jira cross-reference: PC-54225 (Closed) documents the same error pattern for AE region order AE260908-78324187, remediated by re-triggering the consignment process. TKME-2055 and TKME-2089 are similar TR-region tickets.

5 of 6 orders (TR260924-93308617, TR260924-93147668, TR260923-92226009, TR260917-86921245, TR260919-88229034) have the same lifecycle: consignment was CANCELLED at the warehouse (WC12-S751 or WC17-S751), consignment process SUCCEEDED, but the refund FOLLOW_ON call to the Masterpass payment gateway returned ERROR. All order totals are zeroed out (0E-8 TRY). The order process is stuck at RUNNING state, cycling through isWaitForFinancialCompletionRequired, isSecondFIRequired, and isFinancialUpdateRequired task actions.

The refund failure is in the PaymentTransactionEntry with type REFUND_FOLLOW_ON and status ERROR. The Masterpass payment gateway rejected the follow-on refund request. Orders TR260923-92226009, TR260917-86921245, and TR260919-88229034 share the same refund error timestamp (2026-09-25 07:30:26) and the same product (UE32H5000FUXTK x3), indicating a batch refund processing failure.

The 6th order (TR260925-94514044) has a different profile: first consignment CANCELLED at WC12-S751, second consignment stuck at READY status with consignment process RUNNING. The WMS did not process the cancel delivery order for the second consignment. Order total dropped to 1.00 TRY. Payment captured at 450,000 TRY but no refund has been initiated. The cancel email process SUCCEEDED but the second consignment remains blocked.

Jira cross-reference found PC-48853 (Closed) documenting REFUND_FOLLOW_ON PTE update remediation and PC-35580 (Closed) for refund follow-on entry to success. These PC tickets confirm that the standard remediation is to update the PTE status and re-trigger the refund flow.

Pattern 3: Financial process I/O error (2 orders)

TR260925-94391432 (WAITING_FOR_SEND_FINANCIAL): The order process (order-process-v25-69) failed at the splitOrder action with an I/O error: sec.divaportal.com:443 failed to respond. The DIVA portal is the financial integration endpoint for TR region. No consignments were ever created. Payment was captured (69,999 TRY) but the initial FI posting to SAP/GERP through the DIVA portal failed. The order process is in ERROR state.

TR260922-91038821 (WAITING_FOR_FINANCIAL): The consignment was fully completed and delivered (shipped 2026-09-25, GERP bill 3247490146, completed 2026-09-26), but the order process failed at the completeFinancialUpdate action with Connection reset. The order process is in ERROR state. Payment was captured (83,579.99 TRY across 2 transactions) but the second FI (completion FI) failed.

Code trace: SendOrderCompleteFinancialUpdateAction (extends SendInitialFinancialUpdateAction) calls tokoConsignmentFinancialsService.sendInitialFinancialUpdate() at line 22. For TR region, this connects to sec.divaportal.com:443 (DIVA portal). The I/O error occurs when the DIVA portal is unreachable or drops the connection during the FI posting.

Jira cross-reference found TKME-1979 (DIVA portal failure) and TKME-1610 (DIVA services HTTPS update), confirming DIVA portal instability is a known TR-region issue. Monitoring alerts HTCK-4443, HTCK-4048, HTCK-4564 track high failure rates for divaportal.com.

Pattern 4: Refund FOLLOW_ON payment gateway error (1 order)

TR260924-93500425 (REFUND_FAILED): No consignments were ever created. The order process is in FAILED state (not RUNNING). The payment transaction has AUTH=ACCEPTED, CAPTURE=ACCEPTED, and REFUND_FOLLOW_ON=ERROR for 27,139.65 TRY. The order was cancelled before fulfilment and the refund to the Masterpass payment gateway failed immediately. Task logs show the refund path was entered: refundCancelOrder, isChargeBackRefundProcessed, releaseVirtualStock, cancelNonActivatedExternalService, isInstantRefundEnabledCheckBeforeFinancialUpdate.

The REFUND_FOLLOW_ON failure is a payment gateway rejection, not a Hybris code defect. The Masterpass gateway may have rejected the refund due to a processing window restriction, duplicate refund attempt, or gateway-side issue.

Pattern 5: Completed but missing shipping date (1 order)

TR260926-95654349 (COMPLETED): The order is fully COMPLETED. All 5 consignments are COMPLETED, all processes (order, consignment, omnichannel, store email, dispatch email) are SUCCEEDED. GERP bills exist for all consignments. Payment AUTH and CAPTURE accepted (85,119 TRY). However, the first consignment (entry 0, product WW90DG6U25LEAH, a washing machine) has no shipping date despite having a completion date and GERP bill. No tracking IDs exist on any of the 5 consignments.

This is a data integrity issue, not a process error. The consignment was physically delivered and GERP billed, but the shipping date field was never populated by the warehouse subsystem. The order itself is COMPLETED and the process is SUCCEEDED, so no process remediation is needed.

Note: Kibana log analysis was not performed (Kibana MCP was unavailable during this investigation). The error messages cited in the ticket description and the DB state verification provide sufficient evidence for the root cause analysis above. If Kibana becomes available, log analysis could confirm the exact exception stack traces and timestamps.

Possible remediation:

Pattern 1 (Connection reset at sendConsignmentToWarehouse) - 6 orders:
Re-trigger the consignment process from the sendConsignmentToWarehouse action. The consignment data is intact and the WMS connection reset was transient. Reusable PC ticket: PC-52605 (process-restart, REUSABLE, parent TKME-2279, script: script-TKME-2279-retrigger-business-process.groovy). Adapt the script to target these 6 orders' consignment processes, resetting the ERROR state and re-triggering from the sendConsignmentToWarehouse action node. For the 2 partial orders (TR260926-95689021, TR260925-94199293), only retrigger the stuck consignment process (the one in ERROR state), not the completed one.

Pattern 2 (Cancel DO blocked by WMS with refund failure) - 6 orders:
For the 5 REFUND_FAILED orders (TR260924-93308617, TR260924-93147668, TR260923-92226009, TR260917-86921245, TR260919-88229034): The consignments are already CANCELLED and the consignment process SUCCEEDED. The issue is the REFUND_FOLLOW_ON PTE in ERROR state. Remediation: update the PTE status from ERROR to SUCCESS (if the refund was actually processed by the gateway) or re-trigger the refund (if the refund was not processed). Reference: PC-48853 (Closed) and PC-35580 (Closed) document the PTE update approach. Reusable PC ticket: PC-52765 (refund-retrigger, REUSABLE, parent SAME-3941, script: script-SAME-3941-sa260722-return-refund-retrigger.groovy) may be adaptable for the refund retrigger.

For TR260925-94514044 (Cancel DO blocked by WMS without refund): The second consignment is stuck at READY with the consignment process RUNNING. This requires WMS team intervention to either cancel the delivery order or confirm fulfilment. The WMS has blocked the cancel DO and Hybris cannot force this. Once WMS resolves the DO, the consignment process should advance. If WMS confirms the cancel, the refund flow will need to be triggered. This order may need escalation to the WMS/warehouse operations team.

Pattern 3 (Financial process I/O error) - 2 orders:
TR260925-94391432: Re-trigger the order process from the splitOrder action. The DIVA portal timeout was transient. Reusable PC ticket: PC-52605 (process-restart, REUSABLE). The script should target the order process and reset from the splitOrder action node.

TR260922-91038821: Re-trigger the order process from the completeFinancialUpdate action. The consignment is already COMPLETED and delivered. Reusable PC ticket: PC-52605 (process-restart, REUSABLE). The script should target the order process and reset from the completeFinancialUpdate action node.

Pattern 4 (Refund FOLLOW_ON payment gateway error) - 1 order:
TR260924-93500425: The order process is in FAILED state (not ERROR), so process retrigger alone may not work. The refund FOLLOW_ON PTE needs to be investigated. Check with the payment team whether the Masterpass gateway actually processed the refund despite returning ERROR. If the refund was processed, update the PTE to SUCCESS. If not, re-trigger the refund. Reference: PC-48853 (Closed) for PTE update approach.

Pattern 5 (Completed but missing shipping date) - 1 order:
TR260926-95654349: The order is fully COMPLETED and all processes SUCCEEDED. This is a data integrity issue only. If the missing shipping date causes downstream reporting or tracking issues, update the consignment shipping date field to match the completion date. This is a minor data fix and does not require process remediation.

## Remediation

Reusable PC tickets identified:
1. PC-52605 (REUSABLE) - Process restart for Connection reset and Financial I/O errors (Patterns 1 and 3). Script: script-TKME-2279-retrigger-business-process.groovy. Parent: TKME-2279.
2. PC-52765 (REUSABLE) - Refund retrigger for REFUND_FOLLOW_ON errors (Pattern 2). Script: script-SAME-3941-sa260722-return-refund-retrigger.groovy. Parent: SAME-3941.
3. PC-48853 (Closed) - PTE REFUND_FOLLOW_ON update (Pattern 4). Manual approach documented in ticket.
4. PC-54225 (Closed) - Connection reset remediation precedent (AE region).

Orders requiring WMS team escalation:
- TR260925-94514044 (second consignment DO blocked by WMS at READY status)

Orders requiring no remediation:
- TR260926-95654349 (COMPLETED, data integrity issue only)

Investigation gaps:
- Kibana log analysis was not performed (Kibana MCP unavailable). Log confirmation of exact exception stack traces and timestamps is recommended if Kibana becomes available.
- DIVA portal (sec.divaportal.com) connectivity should be verified - TKME-1979 and TKME-1610 document known instability.

solution.excerpt:
# RCA: AEME-6597

Ticket Summary: Stuck in Shipped Status || 29-Sep
Order: AE260921-84726057 (Replacement Order)
Original Order: AE260918-87269668
Generated: 2026-10-05T07:15:00.000Z

Issue:
Replacement order AE260921-84726057 was stuck in SHIPPED status. The consignment was already COMPLETED in the warehouse with GERP billing number 3247304585 generated on 24-Sep, but the order-level status never transitioned to COMPLETED. After initial remediation (moving order to COMPLETED via PC-52596 push-from-shipped script), the reporter noted the order shows 0 value and invoice cannot be generated.

RCA:
The order is a ReplacementOrder created from original order AE260918-87269668 through return request 09280039. The 0 value is by design. The return request subtotal is 0.00 (exchange, not return-with-refund), and the replacement order entry (SM-F976BZWPMEA, Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra 1TB Cream, qty=1) has basePrice=0 and totalPrice=0. The customer already paid 7899 AED on the original order (totalPrice=7899.00, totalTax=376.14), so the replacement carries no monetary charge. This is the standard Samsung Toko exchange/replacement flow confirmed by the business process return-replacement-order-process-v17 which completed all 18 tasks including checkReplacementOrder and processServicesForReplacement.

The order was stuck in SHIPPED because the consignment completed physically (warehouse delivered, GERP billed on 24-Sep) but the Hybris consignment business process did not detect completion and transition the order status. The initial remediation script (PC-52596, script-AEME-6597-push-from-shipped.groovy) correctly pushed the consignment process forward by restarting at isShippedComplete and moved the order to COMPLETED.

The invoice generation issue has two root causes:
1. SMC external service (pk=9168691242923, provider=SMC, serviceProduct=10985570500609) is in UPDATE_ERROR state. The SMC registration/update failed during the replacement order flow. On the original order, the SMC service is in OK state with statusMessage=OK, confirming SMC worked for the original but failed for the replacement.
2. The consignment externalBillingNumber and externalInvoiceNumber are both empty. The GERP billing number (3247304585) and GERP inbound billing number (5025341804) exist, but the external billing step never completed. The external invoice generation appears to depend on SMC service completion.

The original order's consignment also has empty externalBillingNumber and externalInvoiceNumber, but its SMC service is OK. This suggests either (a) external billing is a separate downstream process not yet triggered, or (b) external billing requires SMC to be in a terminal state (UPDATED/REGISTERED) before it can proceed.

Two consignment email processes are in ERROR state (tokoConsignmentDispatchEmailProcess and tokoConsignmentShippingPreparationEmailProcess), but these are non-blocking for the invoice issue.

Possible remediation:
1. Reset the SMC external service from UPDATE_ERROR to NEW and re-trigger ProcessExternalServicesOnConsignmentAction on the consignment process. Use the existing reusable PC-52678 (scplus-reset, script-AEME-6495-scplus-remediation.groovy) pattern adapted for this order.

2. If the SMC UPDATE_ERROR requires clearing stale policy data first, use PC-53305 (smc-reregistration, script-AEME-6500-smc-reregistration-remediation.groovy) for SMC re-registration.

3. After SMC moves to UPDATED/REGISTERED, monitor whether the external billing/invoice number populates automatically. If not, a separate consignment process retrigger may be needed (PC-52605, process-restart pattern).

4. The two email processes in ERROR can be addressed by restarting them or suppressing the notification types, but these are non-blocking for the invoice issue.

Reusable PC tickets identified: PC-52596 (push-to-completed, already applied), PC-52678 (scplus-reset), PC-53305 (smc-reregistration), PC-52605 (process-restart).

Script already applied: script-AEME-6597-push-from-shipped.groovy (PC-52596)

Hi [~t.zaidi@samsung.com] ,

The order AE260901-08628165 has 2 SC+ subscriptions by design (AE AddedServiceConfig for SMC has maxPerOrder=3). Both subscriptions were created from the same Checkout.com token during order placement.

When a user updates card details from the my-orders page, the Checkout.com card update callback flows through TokoCheckoutDotComFacadeImpl.doAuthorize() -> handleSubscriptionOrder() -> updatePaymentInfo(). The updatePaymentInfo() method (line 995) calls getPaymentTransactionForOrderAndPid() which searches the order PaymentTransactions by paymentProvider and paymentId, returning the most recent matching PT. It then gets the subscriptionData from that PT and updates only that single subscription token, paymentInfo, and paymentMode.

All 4 PaymentTransactions on this order are linked to sub1 (ARE26I0411465355) or have no subscriptionData. Zero PTs exist for sub2 (ARE26I0461157598). When the card update callback fires, getPaymentTransactionForOrderAndPid() finds PT4 (created Sep 17, linked to sub1), updates sub1 token successfully, but sub2 is never reached.

The Adyen facade handles this correctly via updateEachSubscriptionData() (line 4523) which iterates all ExternalServiceEntries on the order and updates each subscription token + paymentInfo individually. Checkout.com had no equivalent iteration logic.

We also verified that the manual "_1" appended to the token is not a contributing factor. The token is an output that gets SET from the Checkout.com response source ID, not an input used for PT matching. The subscription ONHOLD status does not block the card update flow either -- the update code does not check subscription status.

Proposed fix: In TokoCheckoutDotComFacadeImpl.updatePaymentInfo(), after updating the matched PT subscription, iterate all remaining subscriptions on the order and call updateSingleSubscriptionPaymentInfo() for each, mirroring Adyen updateEachSubscriptionData() pattern. The existing updateSingleSubscriptionPaymentInfo() method handles the actual update logic per subscription (token, paymentInfo, paymentMode). This is the minimal change that addresses the bug.

Thanks,
Aryan

Same issue. The refund was triggered for 1,539.50 AED (discounted order total including the 190 AED delivery service fee) instead of 1,349.50 AED (product price only). Same delivery mode and same DeliveryServiceEntry of 190 AED in LIVING status.
 
The working comparison order AE260223-04184028 (refund 5,599 AED, correctly excluding the 30 AED delivery fee) does not have a DeliveryServiceEntry at all. Its delivery cost is a DeliveryModeEntry only. This is why it works correctly.
 
The bug is in TokoCalcUtils.calculateDeliveryServiceCostForOrder() which sums all DeliveryServiceEntry costs regardless of their EntryStatus. When the SIT return is posted from NERP without the delivery fee, the method unconditionally adds the 190 AED LIVING DeliveryServiceEntry cost back to the refund. The else branch in calculateFullSITReturnRefund computes: orderTotal - deliveryCost + deliveryServiceCost. For AE260216: 2889 - 190 + 190 = 2889. The delivery service cost cancels out the delivery cost deduction.
 
We also verified the TokoConfigProperty table on S2. There is no refund.delivery.cost.for.sit.ae or refund.product.only.for.sit.ae config entry for the AE store. When these configs are absent, both evaluate to false (Boolean.valueOf(null) = false), which triggers the buggy else branch. Other stores like BH, IN, KW, OM, QA, ZA have refund.delivery.cost.for.sit set to true, which makes the refund equal the full order total intentionally. AE does not have this config, so it falls into the unintended code path.
 
The same bug exists in the partial SIT return path through TokoDefaultDeliveryRefundCalculationStrategyImpl.computeDeliveryServiceRefund(). When called with isStatusCheckRequired=false (which processRefundAmount always does), the Default strategy overrides the DEAD-only filter and refunds all DeliveryServiceEntry entries regardless of status. The V2 strategy (used by CA and DE stores) does not have this bug as it always checks for DEAD status. AE uses the DEFAULT strategy.
 
This is a code defect, not a configuration issue. The fix requires adding an EntryStatus.DEAD filter to calculateDeliveryServiceCostForOrder() and removing the isStatusCheckRequired bypass in the Default delivery refund strategy.
 
We are checking further on the same.
 
Regards

Aryan
